They set their enough to duration field included in the ADS. Now, if B is available for reception, then we send back the CDS. Right? Again, the CDS is a way to inform all the neighbors of B that is going to be engaged in a dialogue. Of course, the CDS is also used to tell Access Point One, I'm available, I'm free, please go ahead to start your data packet transmission. But it is also a way to say to say to all the other nodes, look, I'm going to be engaged in a dialogue. So shut up, don't say anything because otherwise you are going to disturb my reception. Okay. So how do we do that? Because the protocol says, all the nodes that can hear the CDS, it's a control packet, they demodulate the header, and they are going to read the duration field in the CDS. And set their enough based on the value that they read. So everyone who receives the CDS will set its enough duration field included in the CDS. And this means that at the MAC layer, they will consider the channel as busy for all that time.
